Statelessness affects an estimated 15 million people worldwide. No one chooses to be stateless, yet in a world organised around nation-states, those affected are frequently excluded from public life and face significant barriers to healthcare and education.

Statefree World e.V. is Germany’s first charity and advocacy organisation dedicated to supporting people affected by statelessness and raising awareness of the issue. With Omega Wants to Dance, we present a film about the joy of dancing in an iconic setting. Fitzroy, located beneath the S-Bahn arches, provides the perfect atmosphere for a special film evening, with drinks and music following the screening. Berlin dance and style icon Günther Anton Krabbenhöft appears in the film and will take part in a conversation with the director Ramon Tort, moderated by Naciye Stein after the screening.

Omega Wants to Dance
Ramon Tort / Spain / 2025 / 92 min
Dance has always been a tool for self-expression and community building. Following people in Asia, Europe, North America, and Latin America, the film shows how movement shapes identity, belonging, and social change. Together, personal experiences and cultural perspectives illustrate how dance becomes a means of connection and communication, offering insight into the physical, emotional, and social dimensions of being human.

title.rendered: TEMPO GALLERY x STAYGOLD presents: Annina, Ian Zunich, Hyperbole & Franco (ar)

acf.event_description:
Tempo Gallery is coming together with Staygold to release its first ever international party at the Infamous Fitzroy Club. Annina of Zapped Records will be headlining and its just in time for the follow up Saturday from May Day in Berlin.

Heading up the Zapped Records Label, Annina, originally from a small country town in Finland is a track-sourcing weapon. This caused a buzz of chatter in the scene after a string of knock-out DJ performances to a packed Wintergarten (Sisyphos) and iconic Golden Gate closing sets in 2022/2023

Annina has continued to blaze a trail through Berlin and beyond having played at venues such as Hoppetosse, Watergate and Culture Box just to name a few.

Furthering her skills in the studio she is also making an entry into the world of production with multiple release dates set both on Zapped Records, her own independent Bandcamp and other labels.

Following up we have Franco (ar) coming from Tulum he has been travelling all over Europe playing and producing drivey basslines and peaktime moments. His mix of techy, wobbly textures and latin polyrhythms creates a massive sound that brings the club temp up and heavy. His Party series Random Jam has been seen all over the world and brings these sounds to the forefront.

Ian Zunich, Founder of Tempo Gallery will be playing after Annina bringing the crowd into the late night with uplifting acid squelchers mixed in with 90s garage and minimal house groovers. Combining the sound of Berlin with his influence of 90s Detroit and electro emotional electronic tracks.

Ians productions have been recently featured on Echocentric Records out of Helsinki sitting right next to an Eden Burns remix of Capes track coming also from LA, this show will be kicking off his Berlin/New York tour.

Hyperbole will be joining us as well, he is a Berlin-based DJ from Los Angeles. He runs Staygold and is a founding member of Zwischenzeit.

Known for high-energy sets rooted in minimal and progressive house, blending deep, rolling basslines with driving grooves and passionate vocals. Focused on building tension and moving the floor through different shades of house.

title.rendered: SONAR TALK – Berlin nightlife as a FLINTA

acf.event_description:
Berlin Nightlife as FLINTA*

Partying as FLINTA* is anything but easy. Unfortunately, “just” having fun, forgetting about everyday life and switching off is often wishful thinking and not reality. Why is that? What needs to change? Where can we start? Where do the others (cis men) need to do the work? And what role does consumption play when it comes to celebrating as FLINTA*?

We want to create a space to talk about gender-specific challenges, frustrations and emotions such as fear, disgust or anger. But there should be equal space for the beautiful sides, the already existing spaces from the community, moments of cohesion and emotions such as joy or love.
We want to immerse ourselves together in a perhaps almost utopian world and work out what “safe partying” could look like for FLINTA*s.
Grab your friends and let's discuss partying, consumption and the fight against patriarchal structures in Berlin's nightlife!

Our Clubtalks are an open forum for all night owls and sympathizers. The November Clubtalk is aimed exclusively at people who feel they belong to FLINTA* (women, lesbians, inter, non-binary, trans and agender people). The sessions are accompanied and moderated by us. For us, anything goes, but no trashtalk, blaming or any other kind of devaluation of others. Simplification and prejudice are out of place here. Let’s create a safer-space together!

Depending on how it suits everyone present, the club talk will be held in German or English. We will decide together.
